name: Ratboys
label: New West
lede: Two Notre Dame freshmen met in a Facebook group, went through nine drummers, and sixteen years later a therapy exercise gave them the record critics put next to the year's best.

eras.title: A Facebook group and a swimming pool
eras.text: Two Notre Dame students start writing songs as an acoustic duo in dorms, basements and a converted school pool in South Bend. By 2014 a class assignment has pushed them toward electric guitars.

years.src: Notre Dame Magazine · Human Pursuits · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Steiner spots Sagan's bass-playing profile photo on Facebook
years.p: Julia Steiner noticed a funny comment from Dave Sagan in the Notre Dame class-of-2014 Facebook group. They met on campus that fall.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine tells it this way: Steiner saw a funny comment, saw that Sagan's profile photo had him playing bass, and started messaging. Their musical backgrounds differed, and the connection was immediate anyway.

Sagan grew up in Oak Forest, a south suburb of Chicago, and later pulled Steiner into the city's DIY scene. Wikipedia dates the band's formation to fall 2010.

years.src: Notre Dame Magazine · Treble · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Ratboy EP on Swerp Records
years.p: The duo's first release: five lo-fi acoustic sketches, years before the electric guitars showed up.
years.xp:
The name was Steiner's high school nickname, from a lunch-table game where friends handed each other weird names. The plural came after another musician called Ratboy sent them a threatening email about it, per Notre Dame Magazine.

They played wherever South Bend let them: Acousticafe, the Riley Hall art building, a Breen-Phillips basement, the Reckers snack bar, the Mendoza business school courtyard. Steiner says they liked being a little rogue.

years.h: The Pool, a school swimming pool turned apartment
years.p: From 2011 to 2015 a South Bend apartment built in a former school pool hosted the shows that taught Steiner DIY was for her too.
years.xp: Steiner told Notre Dame Magazine that The Pool made her feel comfortable and safe in a DIY environment, and empowered to go looking for that scene elsewhere.

years.h: A class assignment gets louder: "Collected" and "Space Blows"
years.p: Steiner recorded both songs for a class project on women in rock, and the pair came out as May 2014 singles.
years.xp:
The assignment let students write a paper or make a creative project. Steiner chose two original songs about what women face in music, and the band says it pushed them toward louder, electric arrangements.

Both songs reappeared as re-recordings on Happy Birthday, Ratboy in 2021.

eras.title: Basements, nine drummers and a van
eras.text: Topshelf puts out a debut, Sagan graduates, and the band spends two years on the road. A rotating rhythm section finally settles.

years.h: AOID · Topshelf Records
years.p: Recorded at the Owlery in Chicago in late 2014, with Steiner cutting vocals at night so nobody else was in the room.
years.xp:
Mike Politowicz of Dowsing connected the band with Topshelf. Several songs, including "Charles Bernstein" and "Our Mortician's Daughter", had been live staples since mid-2012, and "Postman Song" dated to 2007.

The Chicago Tribune's Kevin Williams called it "almost like a sketch", really good but incomplete. GoldFlakePaint put it on its 2015 year-end list.

years.cap: Ratboys on their first self-booked run.
years.h: 22 basements and bars in 22 days
years.p: After Sagan graduated, the duo booked themselves from Kalamazoo, Michigan to New Orleans.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine quotes the plan as 22 basements and bars in 22 days. The band has funded itself with gig work such as DoorDash and Instacart.

Wikipedia adds that they toured the US and Europe with Pinegrove, Sorority Noise, Free Throw and Dowsing, and put out a 2016 split with Dowsing.

years.h: Nine drummers later, Pet Symmetry's Marcus Nuccio takes the seat
years.p: Sean Neumann became the bassist in 2016; Nuccio came aboard in 2017 after a run of nine drummers, per Paste.
years.xp: Steiner told Treble that a booking agent approached them at a New York show where they were opening for Nuccio's other band, Pet Symmetry: "The fact that anyone wanted to invest their time with working with us was a big turning point for us." Neumann and Sagan both grew up in Chicago's southern suburbs.

yt: Elvis Is in the Freezer (official video)
years.h: GN · Topshelf Records
years.p: Recorded at Atlas Studios with Mike Crotty; Rolling Stone put it on a list of 15 great albums you probably didn't hear in 2017.
years.xp:
Metacritic scores it 77. Steven Hyden picked it among 2017's best at Uproxx, and in 2025 ranked it 98th on his list of the best indie rock albums of the century, calling it "a foundational melding of emo and alt-country."

Wikipedia says the band toured two years behind it across the US, Canada, Europe and Japan, with Soccer Mommy, PUP, Diet Cig and Wild Pink.

eras.title: An empty house in Louisville
eras.text: The lineup that will make every record from here on records its first album together. A pandemic cancels the victory lap.

years.src: Wikipedia: Printer's Devil (album) · Paste · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Printer's Devil · Topshelf Records
years.p: Steiner wrote it at her empty childhood home in Louisville, Kentucky, and the band cut it with Erik Rasmussen at Decade Music Studio in Chicago.
years.xp: It was the first record with the full four-piece. Paste says they had 10 days in the studio. Pitchfork scored it 7.7 and MTV called it the best album of their career. The lead single was "Alien with a Sleep Mask On".

years.h: SXSW is cancelled, so the band starts a Discord
years.p: Three members were living together when COVID hit, and the band kept fans close through a Patreon, a Discord and Twitch streams.
years.xp: Paste reports the cancelled 2020 SXSW slot was meant to celebrate Printer's Devil. The band says the lockdown gave them time to work on new songs together, which shaped the next record.

eras.title: Seattle, on tape
eras.text: A surprise anniversary record, a producer met on tour, a commercial for Walmart, and a support slot that puts them in front of the Decemberists' crowd.

years.h: Happy Birthday, Ratboy · surprise release
years.p: For the 10th anniversary the band re-recorded all five songs from the original Ratboy EP, five more early songs and "Go Outside".
years.xp: Stereogum describes it as an anniversary surprise with the current full lineup filling out the old duo songs. Pitchfork's Pete Tosiello gave it 7.2, saying it "contrasts cozy nostalgia with hard-rocking instincts."

years.h: Opening for Foxing in Montreal, they meet Chris Walla
years.p: Walla, the Death Cab for Cutie founder, had produced Tegan and Sara's The Con, which Steiner had just discovered.
years.xp: Paste reports Walla and the band met when they opened for Foxing in Montreal, then traded voice memos ahead of recording. The Window took 24 days at his Hall of Justice studio in Seattle, against the 10 days spent on Printer's Devil.

years.h: "Go Outside" sells Walmart camping trips
years.p: Walmart used the song in a camping spot in its "So Much More" campaign.
years.xp: Secret Road reports the placement; the band had no comment on that page. Nashville Scene later noted the commercial as a moment that widened their audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Window (Ratboys album) · Paste · Treble
years.h: The Window · straight to tape in Seattle
years.p: Recorded at Chris Walla's Hall of Justice studio, the room Nirvana's Bleach and Sleater-Kinney's Dig Me Out came from, in February 2022.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the title track grew out of Steiner's grandfather being unable to say goodbye to his hospitalized wife, seeing her only through a nursing home window. It was the first record where all four members shaped songs from the start.

Pitchfork scored it 8.0; it made Paste's year-end list at number 5, Stereogum's at 6 and Exclaim!'s at 8. The Chicago Tribune called it the band's most confident, assured version.

years.src: Nashville Scene · Notre Dame Magazine · Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: Support for the Decemberists, then 85 shows of their own
years.p: Ratboys opened the Decemberists' 2024 tour, and Notre Dame Magazine counts 85 shows for the year.
years.xp:
Notre Dame Magazine adds that they've played Lollapalooza. Nashville Scene reports headline dates that November, including a Blue Room set at Third Man Records in Nashville.

Decemberists keyboardist Jenny Conlee ended up playing Hammond organ on their next record.

eras.title: Singing to an empty chair
eras.text: A new label, a cabin in Wisconsin, Steve Albini's old studio and a record about an estrangement. The year's best-reviewed album for a band that started in dorm rooms.

years.src: Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: A Wisconsin cabin, then Steve Albini's Electrical Audio
years.p: They wrote at Driftless Cabin in Richland Center, Wisconsin, then tracked with Chris Walla at Electrical Audio in Chicago.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Walla stressed emotional impact over music theory and arrangement, and that at Electrical Audio they built a Doppler effect with a spinning turntable. Sessions also ran at Rosebud in Evanston.

years.h: Ratboys sign to New West and drop "Light Night Mountains All That"
years.p: Nuccio directed the video, and a North American tour was announced for February 2026.
years.xp: Steiner told Exclaim! her original idea was an ultra-high energy folk song in the style of the Dodos' Visiter, with spooky, pastoral imagery, and that it turned into a rural vision-quest during a Wisconsin writing session. The label move ended a run of five albums on Topshelf.

years.src: Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair · Wikipedia: Ratboys
years.h: Singin' to an Empty Chair · Pitchfork 8.4
years.p: Their sixth album, on New West with Chris Walla producing again. Pitchfork's Ivy Nelson gave it 8.4.
years.xp:
Nelson called it their most emotionally affecting and compositionally advanced songs to date. Stereogum's Tom Breihan wrote that it is "about as good as American indie rock gets." Metacritic lands at 85.

"Anywhere" was written around Sagan's dog's separation anxiety. "Burn It Down" was written during the 2020 George Floyd protests. Guests include Jenny Conlee, cellist Elizabeth Jordan and pedal steel player Andy Krull; Chris Shaw mixed and Heba Kadry mastered.

years.big: "Picture this: You're sitting across from a chair where no one else is sitting."
years.src: NPR: Ratboys · The Line of Best Fit · Wikipedia: Singin' to an Empty Chair
years.h: Where the title comes from
years.p: Steiner told NPR she used the Gestalt therapy exercise to work through a fractured relationship with a loved one; the record ends on a Winnie the Pooh-inspired song.
years.xp: Steiner told NPR's World Cafe about the technique, in which you speak aloud to the empty seat as if the person were there. She told The Line of Best Fit the closing "At Peace in the Hundred Acre Woods" comes from the Pooh stories she read growing up and their friendship dynamics.

years.h: Tiny Desk: three songs, and a third of it is "Black Earth, WI"
years.p: "Penny in the Lake", "What's Right?", then the eight-minute Window centerpiece.
years.xp: See Rock Live counts the set at three songs and about 20 minutes. LemonWire reports the Tiny Desk landed alongside a deluxe edition of the album with a Marked Men cover.
